subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Water Hammer: The Shock in the Pipes
description: A quick win: understand Water Hammer: The Shock in the Pipes.

hook.text: Slam a valve shut and the pipes bang. That bang can burst a pipe.

buildup.text: Moving water has momentum. Stop it suddenly and a pressure wave forms.

discovery.text: The wave bounces back and forth, spiking pressure far above normal levels.

twist.text: Water hammer once burst a section of a city water main, flooding streets.

climax.text: Slow-closing valves and surge tanks absorb the shock and protect pipes.

punchline.text: Stopping water fast hits harder than you'd think.

quiz.question: How do engineers prevent water hammer?
options: By using larger pipes that reduce flow velocity
Slow-closing valves and surge tanks absorb the pressure wave
By adding air bubbles to the water to cushion the flow
